title: mountApplication
summary: Mount a Preact route application or hydrate an existing server-rendered document.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: Pass routes, an optional browser-safe rootModule, and an optional options object. options.hash enables hash history. options.deployment accepts the virtual deployment metadata and protects both the initial lazy import and later navigation. A boolean third argument remains supported for hash routing.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: Returns a Promise<Router>. Mounting waits for the initially matched route module to preload. The returned router exposes navigation, revalidation, fetchers, and disposal. Client-only mounting starts loaders through RouterProvider; the returned promise does not mean every loader has completed.

sections.title: Client-only application
sections.body: Provide a root element in the HTML document. Manually registered routes work without a file-router plugin. Keep route components and client handlers in their normal route modules.

sections.title: Server-rendered document
sections.body: When a non-empty #smolter-data script exists, mounting reads its Hydration payload, restores serialized errors, and hydrates the document rather than rendering into #root. Use the matching server and browser route modules and root layout. Scripts emits the bootstrap payload for renderApplication. Keep server handlers out of the browser root module and use the file-router integration to split server route exports.

sections.title: Navigation and root data
sections.body: Mounting retains the committed view while a new route loads and connects navigation metadata. A rootModule with loaderPath registers root revalidation under rootModule.id or "root". loaderPath must identify a registered data route; mounting does not invent an endpoint. With neither hydration data nor #root, a router is returned but no application is rendered.

sections.title: Bootstrap recovery
sections.body: Pass deployment metadata during mounting; installing watchDeployment only after mounting cannot recover an initial import failure. A failed bootstrap checks for a different build and requests one reload per old build. Offline checks and unchanged builds preserve the original import error. The initial entry script itself must still be available.

sections.title: Externally injected head elements
sections.body: Whole-document hydration expects the server and client layouts to match. Mark externally injected direct children of head with data-smolter-preserve. mountApplication temporarily excludes those nodes from hydration and restores the same nodes afterward; the application must not also render them. This is an explicit integration contract, not automatic tolerance of arbitrary HTML rewriting. Do not use it for application-owned tags, body content, or changes to the hydration payload.
